their_strongest_arguments.argument: The complaint is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties: only the authorised service centre has been impleaded, while the warranty is a contract given by the manufacturer and the sale was by a retailer/seller, neither of whom is before the Commission. No effective order for repair, replacement or refund can be passed against a mere repair agent.
their_strongest_arguments.likely_basis: Warranty card terms naming the manufacturer as warrantor [TO CONFIRM]; invoice showing the selling dealer's name [TO CONFIRM]; settled practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 of arraying manufacturer and seller in warranty claims.

their_strongest_arguments.argument: The defect falls within an express warranty exclusion (physical/liquid damage or unauthorised tampering), so refusal is a contractual entitlement, not a deficiency in service under s.2(11).
their_strongest_arguments.likely_basis: The exclusion clause in the warranty card and the service centre's inspection/diagnosis remarks recorded on the job sheet [TO CONFIRM — exact exclusion cited by the centre is not on record].

their_strongest_arguments.argument: The complainant has led no independent proof of manufacturing defect; under the scheme of the Act an allegation of defect in goods ordinarily requires analysis/testing by an appropriate laboratory, and a bare assertion of 'hardware fault' cannot discharge that burden.
their_strongest_arguments.likely_basis: Section 38(2)(c)-(d) procedure for testing of goods; absence of any expert or second-opinion report in the annexure list.

their_strongest_arguments.argument: Delay is attributable to the complainant, not the opposite party: the handset was retained pending the complainant's refusal to approve a chargeable (out-of-warranty) estimate, and the centre offered paid repair which was declined.
their_strongest_arguments.likely_basis: Job sheet/estimate entries and service centre call logs or SMS records [TO CONFIRM]; no correspondence from the complainant demanding return of the handset is annexed.

their_strongest_arguments.argument: Compensation of Rs 15,000 for 'harassment' is unsubstantiated and speculative; no pleading of actual loss, medical or professional prejudice, or any legal notice putting the opposite party on notice before filing.
their_strongest_arguments.likely_basis: Absence of particulars of loss in the draft and absence of any pre-litigation notice on record [TO CONFIRM whether a notice was issued].

their_strongest_arguments.argument: Territorial jurisdiction and cause-of-action dating are not pleaded with particulars — the draft pleads only the purchase date (15.01.2026) and not the date of handover to the service centre or the date of refusal, leaving the Commission without a pleaded cause of action.
their_strongest_arguments.likely_basis: Section 34(2) territorial jurisdiction requirements; the facts JSON records only 'date_of_cause: 2026-01-15' with no handover or refusal date.

our_rebuttals.rebuttal: Procedural answer only: seek leave to amend the memo of parties and implead the manufacturer and the selling dealer as Opposite Party Nos. 2 and 3 before the first hearing, so the objection is cured at the threshold rather than argued. Non-joinder is in any event not fatal where the Commission can order impleadment.
our_rebuttals.needs_evidence: Warranty card naming the warrantor; tax invoice showing seller's name and full address; manufacturer's registered office address [all TO CONFIRM].

our_rebuttals.rebuttal: Put the opposite party to strict proof: the exclusion must be pleaded with the specific clause number and supported by the written inspection finding communicated to the complainant. If refusal was oral and no written reason was ever given, the burden of proving the exclusion is not discharged.
our_rebuttals.needs_evidence: Job sheet copy with the centre's remarks; any written/email/SMS refusal from the centre; copy of the warranty card clauses; complainant's account of the phone's condition at handover [TO CONFIRM].

our_rebuttals.to: No proof of defect; laboratory testing required
our_rebuttals.rebuttal: Frame the primary grievance as deficiency in service (three months' retention without repair or return) rather than defect in goods, so the testing requirement is not the gateway issue; alternatively, apply under s.38(2)(c) for the Commission to direct testing and offer to deposit the prescribed fee.
our_rebuttals.needs_evidence: Dated job sheet establishing the handover date; any acknowledgement of continued retention; complainant's willingness/ability to deposit testing fee [TO CONFIRM].

our_rebuttals.to: Delay caused by complainant refusing a paid estimate
our_rebuttals.rebuttal: Demand production of the estimate and the complainant's alleged refusal in writing; in any event, retention of the handset for three months without returning it, even on an out-of-warranty finding, is independently pleadable as deficiency.
our_rebuttals.needs_evidence: All communications between client and the centre (SMS, WhatsApp, emails, call records); whether client ever asked for the handset back and was refused [TO CONFIRM].

our_rebuttals.rebuttal: Add particulars to the pleading: dates of deprivation, cost of any substitute handset, and any documented professional/personal prejudice; consider issuing a pre-litigation legal notice, subject to the limitation date on the packet.
our_rebuttals.needs_evidence: Receipts for alternate phone/rental, if any; client's statement of actual loss; copy of any notice already sent [TO CONFIRM].

our_rebuttals.to: Defective pleading of cause of action and jurisdiction
our_rebuttals.rebuttal: Amend the Facts paragraph to plead (i) date of handover to the service centre, (ii) date and mode of refusal, (iii) the address at which the complainant resides or works and the branch address of the opposite party, to ground s.34(2) jurisdiction; recompute the limitation date from the correct cause-of-action date before filing.
our_rebuttals.needs_evidence: Job sheet date; date of refusal; client's residential/work address; service centre branch address [all TO CONFIRM]. NOTE: the packet states a limitation deadline of 2026-09-29 against a cause of action in January 2026 — this apparent mismatch must be verified with the supervising advocate before filing.

parsed.weakest_point_in_our_draft: The draft sues only the service centre and pleads no date of handover and no date or written particulars of the refusal — so on its face it neither identifies the party who owes the warranty obligation nor discloses when the cause of action arose, which exposes it to both a non-joinder objection and a limitation/jurisdiction objection at admission stage.
parsed.settlement_reason: The disputed sum (Rs 40,000 plus Rs 15,000) is modest and the reputational and time cost of contesting a warranty matter usually pushes service centres and manufacturers towards repair or replacement, especially once the manufacturer is impleaded. It is not rated high because the opposite party appears to have taken a firm exclusion-based stand for three months, and the strength of that stand cannot be assessed until the written refusal reason and the warranty clause are on record [TO CONFIRM]. Mediation under s.37 may be explored, but only after the supervising advocate confirms the limitation position.
